Diagnosis.submission: The recommendation service is down because an orphaned ValidatingWebhookConfiguration named pod-policy.validation.k8s.io is blocking pod creation in the hotel-reservation namespace. This webhook has failurePolicy set to Fail and references a service pod-policy-webhook in the policy-system namespace, but that namespace and service do not exist. When the recommendation pod crashed and was killed, the replicaset attempted to recreate it, but the admission webhook rejected the pod creation because the referenced webhook service was unreachable. The result is that the recommendation deployment is stuck at 0/1 replicas available, making the recommendation functionality of the hotel reservation application unavailable.

Diagnosis.submission: The frontend service failed to initialize its gRPC client connections to backend services (search, profile, recommendation, user) because it started before the Consul service discovery was ready. At startup, the gRPC Consul resolver attempted to query Consul for service instances but received connection refused (Consul was not yet listening on port 8500). As a result, the gRPC connections were established with zero backend endpoints. The gRPC resolver did not recover/retry successfully, so all subsequent requests to the frontend that required gRPC calls to backend services (particularly the SearchHandler CheckAvailability call to the search service) failed. The root cause is a startup race condition between the frontend deployment and the Consul service, where the frontend does not wait for Consul to be available before initializing its gRPC load-balanced connections.

This new revision adds WAF rule evaluation (WAF_RULE_REGEX and WAF_RULE_ENABLED environment variables) and only forwards requests to the frontend service. The original frontend-proxy (revision 1) did not have these WAF rules. Additionally, during startup, the product-catalog service experienced a restart due to a race condition with PostgreSQL initialization, and the frontend logged a transient ECONNREFUSED error connecting to the checkout service. The primary fault is the frontend-proxy being modified to include WAF rules in its request handling path.

Diagnosis.submission: The frontend-proxy service has a misconfigured environment variable FRONTEND_HOST set to localhost (instead of the correct value frontend) in its deployment. This extra environment variable was added to the deployment, causing the Envoy proxy to route requests to localhost:8080 instead of the frontend Kubernetes service at frontend:8080. This breaks the application because the frontend-proxy cannot reach the actual frontend service. Additionally, the product-catalog pod crashed twice on startup (exit code 1) due to a race condition where it started before PostgreSQL was ready, as it lacks a wait-for-postgresql init container.

Diagnosis.submission: The nginx-thrift pod (OpenResty Thrift RPC proxy) in the social-network namespace was being OOMKilled due to insufficient memory (16Mi limit). The root cause is a mutating admission webhook called platform-policy-controller (running in the platform-ops namespace, registered as gatekeeper-mutating-webhook-configuration) that intercepts all pod creations in the social-network namespace and unconditionally overrides the container memory resources to 16Mi, overriding the deployment-specified 256Mi limit. This caused the nginx-thrift proxy to be OOMKilled on every start, breaking the Thrift RPC communication layer between microservices. The fix was to delete the gatekeeper-mutating-webhook-configuration mutating webhook configuration and recreate the nginx-thrift pod with its correct 256Mi memory limit.

Diagnosis.submission: The search deployment is down (0/1 replicas) because a ResourceQuota named memory-limit-quota with a hard memory limit of 1Gi was applied to the hotel-reservation namespace. The search container (hotel-reserv-search) does not specify memory limits or requests in its resource configuration (only CPU limits are defined). Kubernetes quota admission control requires that all containers specify memory resources when a memory quota is set in the namespace. The pg_hba.conf requires scram-sha-256 authentication for all non-localhost TCP connections, but the password stored for user "otelu" in PostgreSQL does not validate correctly via SCRAM-SHA-256. The fix was to remove the malicious template rule from the CoreDNS Corefile ConfigMap and restart CoreDNS to clear negative DNS caches.
